Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the SIG intake. We are finishing the MedAlign SIG v2 and need written answers and evidence for a handful of data-treatment items before our risk committee review next week. Specifically we need clarity on:
- Whether Redwood ever trains models on customer prompt/response logs or derivatives (embeddings, model summaries) absent explicit contract opt-in;
- Retention windows for raw prompt logs, model outputs, and any derived artifacts (embeddings/semantic indexes);
- Whether derivatives generated from customer data are treated as customer data and subject to deletion requests;
- How KV/prefix caches are retained for streaming or low-latency inference; and
- Options for customers to opt-out of any training or analytics that use their data.

Can you provide a short formal response for inclusion in the SIG and a small evidence bundle (docs/controls/screenshots) that we can attach to the SIG? We’ve put an internal target of EOD Thursday (5/13) to have formal language. If helpful, happy to jump on a quick call.

Vanessa / team,

Draft language below intended for insertion into the SIG (concise, factual). I’ve attached a draft evidence PDF (sig_response_v1.pdf) and a retention matrix we can share as an exhibit. Please review and comment.

DRAFT SIG RESPONSES (high level):
1) Training on customer content: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response logs or customer-provided data to train or improve any models by default. Customer data is only used for model training or evaluation with an explicit contractual opt-in and documented agreement.

2) Retention of prompts & outputs: For Hosted customers, request/response logs used for debugging and billing are retained by default for 30 days. Customers can request shorter retention or deletion via support. For Dedicated and Private deployments, retention is configurable and controlled by the customer; Redwood does not retain copies beyond the customer's configured retention for Private deployments.

3) Derivatives (embeddings, semantic indexes, summaries): Derivatives produced from customer content are treated as customer data. They are subject to the same deletion and export controls as raw data. We include deletion endpoints in our platform APIs and will include a short sample in the evidence bundle.

4) KV / prefix cache behavior: By default, transient KV caches used for low-latency streaming are ephemeral (default TTL = 2 minutes) and exist in-memory on serving nodes. We provide optional configurable prefix caching (e.g., for reuse of context) with user-settable TTLs up to 24 hours for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private deployments can set TTLs per policy.

5) Opt-out and governance: Customers may opt-out of any use of their data for training via contract or self-serve controls in the Console (for hosted accounts). Opt-out flags are enforced at the service layer; any opt-in for training is logged and requires dual-approval workflow and a contract amendment.

Notes: I referenced SOC 2 controls for access/review in the evidence PDF. Karthik — please check the TTL wording and add encryption/controls text.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: SIG draft — technical clarifications

Quick technical clarifications and suggested tweak to the KV cache paragraph for the SIG:
- KV cache: default TTL for in-memory streaming cache is 2 minutes (ephemeral), designed to keep per-request KV entries local to the serving cluster. We also maintain an optional fast prefix cache (configurable) that can be persisted to encrypted object storage for reuse; typical hosted configs use 1–24 hour TTLs depending on workload.
- Storage and encryption: all persisted logs/derivatives at rest are encrypted with customer-segregated keys where available; we use KMS-backed keys (AES-256) and integrate with customer-managed keys for Private deployments.
- Training pipeline: there are multiple technical gates before any customer data could be routed to a training pipeline (contractual flag + access control + staging isolation). No automated path exists that routes customer prompts into public training corpora.

Suggested wording addition: add a line confirming that derivatives generated within a customer's private deployment never leave that deployment unless explicitly exported by the customer.

-Karthik

Thank you for the clear list. Please find Redwood's formal responses below (for copy/paste into the SIG) and an attached evidence bundle (redwood_sig_evidence_pack_v3.zip) that includes: control screenshots, SOC 2 summary, sample API deletion call, and our retention matrix. If you need an expanded artifact set (logs, config screenshots for a sandbox), tell me what you need and we’ll produce it.

FORMAL RESPONSES FOR SIG: (concise)
1) Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response logs or derivatives to train or improve our public models by default. Any use of customer data for training requires explicit, written, contractual opt-in and a documented dual-approval workflow.

2) Retention policy: Hosted (default): transient in-memory KV cache for streaming (default TTL = 2 minutes). Standard hosted request/response logs retained for 30 days by default for debugging, monitoring, and billing. Customers may request shorter retention or deletion. Dedicated/Private: retention is customer-configurable; Redwood does not retain secondary copies beyond the configured retention for Private deployments. See attached retention matrix for specifics.

3) Treatment of derivatives: Artifacts derived from customer content (including embeddings, semantic indexes, and summaries) are treated as customer data. They are subject to deletion, export, and access controls identical to raw inputs. For Private deployments, derivatives remain within the customer boundary unless explicitly exported.

4) Opt-out controls: Customers can opt-out of any use of their data for training via contract amendments or self-serve settings in the Console (hosted accounts). Opt-in for training requires documented approval and a contract amendment.

5) Security & controls: Persisted logs and derivatives are encrypted at rest with KMS-backed keys; Private deployments support customer-managed keys. Access to logs is role-based and audited. Our SOC 2 Type II report and control screenshots are included in the evidence bundle.

Next steps: happy to join your vendor risk call. I’m available Fri 5/14 10–12 PT and Mon 5/17 09–11 PT. What works for your team?

Regards,
